intent: What does a Denver-area gym, training studio or school need to settle before putting turf on an indoor floor: which building and fire code editions and which office or fire district cover the address, whether a Denver space changing use needs an architect and a new certificate of occupancy, and where a public or charter school gets its permit?
distinctValue: The national indoor-turf page and the /blog/indoor-turf-for-a-gym/ article cover layout, pad, the Section 804 floor-covering tests, occupancy groups and the sprinkler exception, and the Grand Strand and northeast Florida pages cover other states. This page gives only the Denver-metro layer: an address-by-address map of code editions, checked 12 September 2026. Denver builds on the 2024 IBC and IFC with 2025 city amendments (ordinance 25-0735, June 2025; CB25-1634, passed 24 November 2025). Westminster lists 2021 building and fire codes in effect since June 1, 2024; Aurora lists 2021 editions; Broomfield adopted 2024 codes including fire, effective April 15, 2026; Thornton's 2024 building codes apply to permit applications from July 1, 2026; Castle Rock lists 2024 building and fire codes for new permit submittals; Erie runs a 2021 building code with a 2024 fire code (adopted as the fire district adopted it) from April 24, 2026. Fire districts: West Metro Fire Rescue does plan review and lists 2021 for Lakewood, 2024 for unincorporated Jefferson County and 2018 for unincorporated Douglas County, and warns that some unincorporated Jefferson County properties carry a city or town mailing address; South Metro Fire Rescue adopted the 2024 IFC for unincorporated Jefferson County on 4 May 2026 while its 2021 IFC stays in effect for unincorporated Arapahoe County; Douglas County's own Building Division lists 2024 building codes effective July 1, 2026 and the 2024 IFC adopted July 14, 2026, which conflicts with West Metro's 2018 listing, so the page tells readers to ask both. Denver-specific: Section 133.1 item 2.D leaves a change of use or occupancy (and egress changes and occupant increases) out of the interior alterations that may be drawn without an architect or engineer; Section 142.2 bars a new occupancy until a new certificate of occupancy is issued; Section 130.3 item 9 exempts floor coverings and carpeting from permits but requires Chapter 8 compliance. Schools: the state Division of Fire Prevention and Control requires a permit; its adopted-codes page lists 2021 editions while West Metro's table lists the 2024 IFC for the state public schools program, so the page tells school readers to ask the Division.

The host refused connections from the research network on 12 September 2026 (curl timed out, WebFetch ECONNREFUSED), so the text was read from the Internet Archive capture and the Legistar December 2025 copy listed next; the quoted sections are identical in both.
supports: 2025 DENVER BUILDING CODE June 2025, 1st Printing November 2025, 2nd Printing (title page of the Internet Archive copy)
The 2024 International Building Code adopted in D.R.M.C. Sec. 10-16 is amended in the following particulars

130.3 Exempted Work. The following construction is exempt from the permit requirements of this code (see Appendix S Section 1.4 of the Denver Commercial Building Code for airport requirements). Exemption from permit requirements of this code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner that violates the provisions of this code or any other laws or ordinances of the City.
9. Painting, papering, tiling, floor coverings, countertops, carpeting, cabinets, curtains, drapes, and similar decoration items. Such items shall comply with Chapter 8.

142.2 Certificate of Occupancy Required. New buildings except Group U occupancy detached private garages and Denver Residential Code non-habitable accessory structures shall not be used or occupied in whole or in part until a Certificate of Occupancy is issued by the building official. No building or portion thereof shall be used or occupied for any occupancy other than the one designated on the Certificate of Occupancy until a new Certificate of Occupancy is issued by the building official.

133.1 Limitations ... 1. Architect or Engineer required. Construction documents for all buildings, structures, additions, alterations, or repairs shall bear the seal and signature of the licensed design professional responsible for each design phase except as provided in the following subsection. ... 2. Architect not required. ... D. Nonstructural, interior, architectural alterations of any nature to a building or tenant space if such alterations do not affect the life safety of the occupants of the building or tenant space. Alterations that do affect the life safety of the building or tenant space include but are not limited to: change of use or change of occupancy; modifications to any part of the means of egress; increase in the number of occupants; modifications to the fire alarm or fire suppression systems

Scope note: the page says Denver's code lets 'many interior alterations' be drawn without an architect or engineer (item 2.D covers nonstructural interior architectural alterations that do not affect life safety) and paraphrases 'modifications to any part of the means of egress' as 'changes to the exits'. It does not say every gym conversion is a change of use; it tells the reader to ask Denver's building department.

sources.label: Colorado SB24-081, signed act (2024), leg.colorado.gov download
supports: SECTION 5. In Colorado Revised Statutes, add 25-15-605 as follows: 25-15-605. Prohibition on the installation of artificial turf that contains intentionally added PFAS chemicals. (1) ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2026, A PERSON SHALL NOT INSTALL ARTIFICIAL TURF THAT CONTAINS INTENTIONALLY ADDED PFAS CHEMICALS ON ANY PORTION OF PROPERTY IN THE STATE.

Supports only the page's closing link to /blog/does-artificial-turf-contain-pfas/ for 'Colorado’s rule on new turf'. The rule is covered in full on denver-metro--turf-removal-and-replacement and the PFAS article, so the page no longer quotes it.

notUsed: Section 804 floor-covering tests (exception, DOC FF-1 pill test or ASTM D2859, testing with underlayment, Class II in corridors for Groups A and B, sprinkler exception) and the Chapter 3 occupancy groups (gymnasiums in A-3, training in B). Denver leaves these as the ICC published them, so they are the same in every area on the International Codes and already appear on the northeast Florida page and in /blog/indoor-turf-for-a-gym/. The page now asks the reader to take those questions to the office and links the article. UpCodes copies of Denver Chapters 3 and 8 are no longer cited.

Denver Fire Code 105.5.33 floor-finishing permit (350 square feet, Class I or II liquids) and 103.1 (Denver Fire Department Prevention Division). The permit is standard International Fire Code text, not a Denver amendment, and no source says whether gluing turf counts. The page keeps only a question: ask whether gluing the turf down needs a fire permit.

Places-of-assembly permit: the June 2025 Denver Fire Code (105.5.64) required an operational permit to operate a place of assembly, but the December 2025 redline strikes it and marks the section Reserved. The page makes no assembly-permit claim.
SB24-081 wording and the PFAS FAQ: already covered on denver-metro--turf-removal-and-replacement, denver-metro--sports-field-turf and /blog/does-artificial-turf-contain-pfas/. Replaced with a link.

Section 142.2 (new certificate of occupancy for a new occupancy) matches the model building code's certificate-of-occupancy rule; it is kept in one sentence only because it pairs with Denver's own 133.1 architect rule in the lease advice, and the page does not present it as unique to Denver.

South Metro Fire Rescue's code edition in its Douglas and Arapahoe County towns (for example Highlands Ranch, Castle Pines, Lone Tree, Parker, Centennial): southmetro.org/721/Adopted-Fire-Codes returned HTTP 404 on 12 September 2026, and the board packet names only unincorporated Jefferson and Arapahoe counties. The page does not say which South Metro edition applies elsewhere.

Highlands Ranch's status: the site's research record lists it as unincorporated Douglas County, but no primary source was opened this session (highlandsranch.org returned 403), so the page speaks of 'outside a town in Douglas County' without naming Highlands Ranch.

Boulder, Arvada, Lakewood's building department, Englewood, Centennial, Littleton and Commerce City code editions were not confirmed (Lakewood and Boulder pages returned 403 or 404 and the web-search budget was exhausted). The page gives those readers a start-with-your-building-department FAQ.
southmetrofire.org/ordinances is the South Metropolitan Fire Protection District in Raymore, Missouri, not South Metro Fire Rescue in Colorado; not used.
Altitude and climate: no primary source ties Denver's elevation or dry air to indoor turf or floor-finish rules, so the page says nothing about climate.
Colorado SB24-005 and HB25-1113 limit artificial turf in outdoor landscapes; whether they reach an indoor floor was not researched, so the page does not mention them.
